content.title: About
content.content: Pasta, vegetable, cooked is a ready‑to‑eat product consisting of boiled pasta mixed with vegetable ingredients (such as carrots, broccoli, tomatoes) and often seasoned with herbs and spices. It is convenient for quick meals and can be served as a main dish or a side.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Vegetable pasta is often made from whole‑grain flour, increasing its nutritional value.
A variety of vegetables can be included, making the dish richer in vitamins and minerals.
These ready‑made mixes are widely used in school cafeterias and office canteens to save time.
The pasta can be fortified with extra plant proteins like soy or pea protein.
There are many regional versions, e.g., Italian pasta with tomato‑vegetable sauce or Asian noodles with vegetable stir‑fry.

items.title: Rich source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Pasta provides sustained energy and a feeling of fullness thanks to the slow release of glucose.

items.title: Contains vegetables
items.content: The vegetable component adds vitamins (A, C, K) and minerals (potassium, magnesium) as well as antioxidants.

items.title: Source of plant protein
items.content: When combined with legumes or soy, the dish becomes a good source of plant‑based protein.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Fiber from whole‑grain pasta and vegetables promotes healthy bowel function.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Compared with many meat‑based meals, vegetable pasta typically contains little saturated fat.

items.title: Gluten content
items.content: Traditional wheat pasta contains gluten, making it unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Salt and additives
items.content: Prepared mixes may have high sodium levels and food additives, so check the label.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: Some recipes include nuts, soy, or dairy, which are common allergens.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: While moderate in calories, large portions can contribute to weight gain.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat the pasta in the microwave or on the stove, add fresh herbs, cheese, olive oil, or a protein‑rich sauce. It works well as a standalone meal, a side to meat or fish, and can be tossed into salads.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked vegetable pasta in the refrigerator at 0–4 °C in an airtight container for up to 3–4 days. For longer keeping, freeze in portion‑size bags for up to 2 months. Discard if it develops off‑odors or an unusual appearance.
